content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text rules on whether witnesses on a side's 'cited in' line count as unanswered for D2 vs C3, which is the counting question K-G4 governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds ((DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 quoting Matthew 1:18, 1:25 and Deuteronomy 22:24; (DR3) C4 quoting Luke 1:34), so the \"witness left unanswered\" ground fails", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.", "room": "'pressed against that link' could mean the verse is quoted in a later round that answers it, or that an earlier round's pressing sentence is quoted; I weighed both readings, and the rule's text requires the second, since it demands quoting the pressing sentence of an earlier round.", "why": "The judge sets aside the unanswered-witness ground by naming verses that later challenger rounds quote, without quoting any earlier-round sentence that pressed them against C3, and the report itself is truncated mid-clause, so the rule's required quote-and-name test is not carried out."}
